title: Design a Library Management System
relevance: High — classic OOD / LLD question (campus + experienced); probes Book vs BookItem, State for copy lifecycle, Strategy for search/fines, Observer for holds, and concurrency on checkout.
company_notes: Very common campus/new-grad OOD/LLD or machine-coding warm-up in India (Flipkart/Uber/Amazon-style loops); SDE-2 follow-ups harden Book vs BookItem, State vs enum, holds, Fine Strategy, per-copy concurrency; FAANG OOD whiteboard classic (Google lore); among the most asked inventory-style LLD templates for resource+copy+reservation domains.

phases.goal: Clarify scope and lock mandatory FR/NFR before drawing classes.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: add books with copies, register members, search catalog, checkout available copy, return copy, enforce borrow limit and loan duration.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists add/register/search/checkout/return plus borrow-limit and loan-duration enforcement as must-haves.

must_hit.point: Ask clarifying questions: physical only or e-books, multi-branch, member tiers, max books and loan days, fines/cap, reservations/renewals, search axes, concurrency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks through clarifying Qs before coding rather than assuming a fixed feature set.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: single branch unless told otherwise, physical copies first, in-memory catalog OK for LLD, one open loan per copy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly calls out single-branch, physical-first, in-memory, one-loan-per-copy assumptions.

must_hit.point: NFR: correct under concurrent checkout; extensible item types and search/fine policies; modular design (not one god class); working demo/CLI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions concurrency correctness, extensibility of types/policies, modularity, and demo as non-functionals.

probes: What are the mandatory functional requirements versus common extensions you would ask about?
Physical copies only, or e-books and multi-branch too?

hints.1: Separate must-have circulation flows from optional holds/fines/roles.
hints.2: Mandatory FR is catalog + members + search + checkout/return + borrow/loan limits; extensions are hold/renew/fines.
hints.3: Clarify physical vs e-book, branch, tiers, limits, fines, holds, search axes, concurrency; assume single branch, physical first, in-memory, one loan per copy.

phases.goal: Name the core entities and the Book vs BookItem split that loans attach to.

must_hit.point: Book/LibraryItem is catalog metadata (ISBN, title, authors); BookItem/BookCopy is a physical copy (barcode/copyId, rack, status).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Clearly separates metadata title from physical copy identity and status.

must_hit.point: Loans attach to a copy, never to the abstract book; Member.borrow(Book) is the classic fail.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says checkout/loan is on BookCopy/BookItem, and calls out borrow(Book) as wrong.

must_hit.point: Hold/reservation waitlist attaches to the Book/LibraryItem (any returned copy can fulfill), not a specific copy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places the queue on the title/item metadata entity, not on one BookItem.

must_hit.point: Supporting entities include Member/Librarian (Account), Loan/BookLending, Catalog, Fine, optional Rack; copy states Available/CheckedOut/OnHold (and Lost).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Member/Librarian, Loan, Catalog, Fine/Rack optionally, and the copy lifecycle states.

probes: What is the difference between Book and BookItem, and what does a loan point to?
Where does the reservation queue live — on the book or on a copy?

hints.1: Think catalog metadata versus something you can put a barcode on.
hints.2: LibraryItem/Book holds ISBN/title; BookCopy holds barcode and status; loans bind to the copy.
hints.3: Book = metadata; BookItem/BookCopy = physical copy; loans on copy; waitlist on Book so any returned copy can fulfill.

phases.goal: Sketch the facade, item/copy hierarchy, State, and Strategy/Observer wiring.

must_hit.point: LibraryManagementSystem/LibraryManager is a Facade orchestrating catalog, members, copy registry, checkout/return/hold/search.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a single entry facade that coordinates subsystems rather than dumping logic everywhere.

must_hit.point: BookCopy delegates transitions to ItemState (Available | CheckedOut | OnHold) so illegal ops like return while available are impossible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws State objects on the copy and routes checkout/return/hold through the current state.

must_hit.point: LibraryItem observes/holds a Member waitlist; ItemFactory creates Book vs Magazine; SearchStrategy and FineStrategy are pluggable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Observer waitlist on LibraryItem, Factory for media types, Strategy for search and fines.

must_hit.point: Relationships: LibraryItem 1..* BookCopy; BookCopy 0..1 Loan → Member; Catalog search indexes; optional Account hierarchy Member|Librarian.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows 1-to-many copies, optional active loan to member, catalog indexes, and role accounts.

probes: Walk me through the class diagram and which patterns each class uses.
How does BookCopy interact with ItemState on checkout and return?

hints.1: Start from facade + item/copy + member, then add patterns for lifecycle and search.
hints.2: Facade owns catalog/members; LibraryItem has copies and hold observers; BookCopy has ItemState; strategies plug into search/fines.
hints.3: LibraryManagementSystem facade; LibraryItem+Factory+Observer holds; BookCopy→ItemState; SearchStrategy/FineStrategy; Loan keyed by copy.

phases.goal: Name the API and the checkout/return/hold flows with lending rules.

must_hit.point: Core API: addItem/addBookItem, registerMember, search, checkout(memberId, copyId), returnItem(copyId), placeHold(memberId, itemId); optional renew and calculateFine/collectFine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the key methods with checkout/return/hold signatures matching the research API.

must_hit.point: On return: if hold observers exist, move copy to ON_HOLD and notify next member; else AVAILABLE.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes return branching on nonempty waitlist → OnHold+notify, else Available.

must_hit.point: Lending rules: max books issued often 5, max lending days often 10–14; reject reference-only items; unpaid-fine threshold before new loans as extension.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States borrow-count and loan-day limits using the file’s 5 and 10–14 figures, plus reference-only reject.

must_hit.point: FineStrategy.calculate(daysOverdue, member, item) — never bury rate math inside returnBook; cap at replacement cost if asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts fine calculation in FineStrategy rather than inside returnItem.

probes: Implement checkout and return — what happens if a hold queue is waiting?
What lending limits and reference-only checks do you enforce at checkout?

hints.1: Name the facade methods first, then narrate return’s hold branch.
hints.2: checkout(memberId, copyId) and returnItem(copyId); on return check observers before AVAILABLE.
hints.3: API as listed; return → ON_HOLD+notify if waitlist else AVAILABLE; limits often 5 books / 10–14 days; FineStrategy outside returnBook.

phases.goal: Show OCP/SRP via Strategy, Factory, and split responsibilities.

must_hit.point: Search via search(query, SearchStrategy) / inverted indexes — don’t forever if(byTitle) inside the facade (OCP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds SearchStrategy (or indexes selected by strategy) instead of growing facade conditionals.

must_hit.point: New media types (magazines/e-books/audiobooks) via LibraryItem hierarchy + ItemFactory; e-books may use license count instead of physical scarcity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Extends with subtypes + Factory and notes license-count for e-books.

must_hit.point: Different fine rates for student vs faculty via FineStrategy (or member-type policy), not if-branches inside returnItem.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Swaps FineStrategy/policy by member tier without editing returnItem.

must_hit.point: SOLID: SRP splits catalog ≠ lending ≠ notifications; DIP depends on SearchStrategy/ItemState/FineStrategy abstractions; avoid god-class Library.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out SRP split and depending on abstractions; rejects one class that searches, bills, notifies, and persists.

probes: How would you add magazines and different student/faculty fine rates without editing the facade’s return path?
Where does Strategy help search stay open for extension?

hints.1: New behavior should plug in, not grow if-else in the facade.
hints.2: Factory for item types; SearchStrategy/FineStrategy for policies; keep catalog/lending/notifications separate.
hints.3: LibraryItem+ItemFactory; search(query, SearchStrategy); FineStrategy for tiers; SRP/DIP — no god-class Library.

phases.goal: Prevent double-checkout of the last copy with the right lock granularity.

must_hit.point: Two librarians must not checkout the same last copy — race on read-then-write status; prefer synchronized(bookCopy) or atomic status CAS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the double-checkout race and locks/CAS on the specific copy.

must_hit.point: ConcurrentHashMap for catalogs/members is necessary but not sufficient — map alone ≠ atomic occupy; still lock per BookCopy checkout.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says concurrent maps help registries but checkout still needs per-copy synchronization.

must_hit.point: Coarse lock on the whole library works for demos but serializes all desks; per-copy lock shows senior thinking.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts global library lock (correct but serializing) with per-copy lock.

probes: Two members checkout the last copy at once — how do you make that safe?
Is ConcurrentHashMap enough for correct checkout?

hints.1: The bug is check-then-act on copy status, not missing a concurrent map.
hints.2: Synchronize or CAS the BookCopy; catalog ConcurrentHashMap alone is not enough.
hints.3: synchronized(bookCopy) or compareAndSet status; ConcurrentHashMap for maps only; avoid coarse whole-library lock except demos.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Skipping the split means you cannot track which copy is damaged/lost or fulfill holds correctly — call Book/LibraryItem (metadata) vs BookItem/BookCopy (physical) out first; loans attach to copies.
Enum + switches ships faster; State wins when transitions/guards grow (e.g. hold-only checkout). Prefer State in OOD rounds; enum OK if timeboxed with centralized transitions.
Book-level queue is correct because any returned copy can satisfy the hold; item-level waitlist breaks when a different copy returns first.
synchronized checkout on the whole library is correct but serializes desks; per-copy lock/CAS addresses the double-checkout race without locking unrelated desks.
Tutorials often Singleton the library/manager; prefer injecting a single instance for testability unless the interviewer wants classic Singleton.

gotchas.trap: Two members checkout the last copy at once
gotchas.correction: Race on read-then-write status — synchronize or compareAndSet on the copy; ConcurrentHashMap alone does not make occupy atomic.

gotchas.trap: Modeling Member.borrow(Book) or attaching loans to metadata
gotchas.correction: Loans attach to BookItem/BookCopy; Book/LibraryItem is catalog metadata only.

gotchas.trap: Reservation queue only on one BookItem
gotchas.correction: Queue lives on Book/LibraryItem so any returned copy can fulfill; item-level waitlist is wrong.
Use LibraryItem hierarchy + Factory; e-books may track license count instead of physical scarcity.

gotchas.trap: Different fine rates with ifs inside returnItem
gotchas.correction: Use FineStrategy (or member-type policy); keep rate math out of returnBook.

gotchas.trap: Renew when someone else holds the title
gotchas.correction: Reject renew; optionally force return into ON_HOLD and notify the waiter.

gotchas.trap: Reference-only / rare books treated like normal copies
gotchas.correction: Flag on copy (e.g. is_reference_only); checkout returns false.

gotchas.trap: God-class Library that searches, bills, notifies, and persists
gotchas.correction: Split SRP across catalog, lending, notifications — interviewer docks design score otherwise.

gotchas.trap: Finishing optional notifications before mandatory flows
gotchas.correction: Ship checkout/return/search first; optional notifications are secondary.
